tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why does the woman say she can be so energetic?

options.A: She can devote all her life to pursuing her passion.
options.B: Her accumulated expertise helps her to achieve her goals.
options.C: She can spread her academic ideas on a weekly TV show.
options.D: Her research findings are widely acclaimed in the world.

questions.cn: 女士为什么说她能这么有精力？

optionsCn.A: 她能毕生追求自己的热情所在。
optionsCn.B: 她积累的专业知识帮助她实现目标。
optionsCn.C: 她能在一档每周播出的电视节目上传播学术观点。
optionsCn.D: 她的研究成果广受世界赞誉。

questions.stem: What has the woman been engaged in?

options.A: Provision of guidance for nuclear labs in Europe.
options.B: Touring the globe to attend science TV shows.
options.C: Overseeing two research groups at Oxford.
options.D: Science education and scientific research.

questions.cn: 女士一直从事什么工作？

optionsCn.A: 为欧洲的核实验室提供指导。
optionsCn.B: 环游全球参加科学电视节目。
optionsCn.C: 监督牛津的两个研究小组。
optionsCn.D: 科学教育与科学研究。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about the benefit teaching brings to her?

options.A: A better understanding of a subject.
options.B: A stronger will to meet challenges.
options.C: A broader knowledge of related fields.
options.D: A closer relationship with young people.

questions.cn: 关于教学带给她的益处，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 对一个学科更好的理解。
optionsCn.B: 迎接挑战的更强意志。
optionsCn.C: 对相关领域更广的知识。
optionsCn.D: 与年轻人更紧密的关系。

questions.stem: How does the woman say new scientific breakthroughs can be made possible?

options.A: By applying the latest research methods.
options.B: By making full use of the existing data.
options.C: By building upon previous discoveries.
options.D: By utilizing more powerful computers.

questions.cn: 女士说怎样才能实现新的科学突破？

optionsCn.A: 应用最新的研究方法。
optionsCn.B: 充分利用现有数据。
optionsCn.C: 在已有发现之上继续构建。
optionsCn.D: 使用更强大的计算机。

lines.t: Conversation 1.
lines.cn: 对话一。

lines.t: M: You are a professor of physics at the University of Oxford.
lines.cn: M：你是牛津大学的物理学教授。

lines.t: M: You're a senior advisor at the European Organization for Nuclear Research.
lines.cn: M：你也是欧洲核子研究组织的高级顾问。

lines.t: M: You also seem to tour the globe tirelessly, giving talks.
lines.cn: M：你还似乎不知疲倦地环游全球，做演讲。

lines.t: M: And, in addition, you have your own weekly TV show on science.
lines.cn: M：另外，你还有一档每周播出的科学电视节目。

lines.t: M: Where do you get the energy?
lines.cn: M：你的精力是从哪里来的？

lines.t: F: Oh, well, I just love what I do.
lines.cn: F：哦，我只是热爱我做的一切。

lines.t: F: I'm extremely fortunate to have this life, doing what I love doing.
lines.cn: F：能有这样的生活，做我热爱的事情，我感到非常幸运。

lines.t: M: Professor, what exactly is your goal?
lines.cn: M：教授，你的目标究竟是什么？

lines.t: M: Why do you do all of this?
lines.cn: M：你为什么做这一切？

lines.t: F: Well, as you said, I do have different things going on, but these, I think, can be divided into two groups, the education of science and the further understanding of science.
lines.cn: F：嗯，正如你所说，我确实同时在做不同的事，但我想这些事可以分为两类：科学教育和科学的进一步理解。

lines.t: M: Don't these two things get in the way of each other?
lines.cn: M：这两件事不会互相妨碍吗？

lines.t: M: What I mean is, doesn't giving lectures take time away from the lab?
lines.cn: M：我的意思是，做讲座不会占用实验室的时间吗？

lines.t: F: Not really, no.
lines.cn: F：真的不会。

lines.t: F: I love teaching, and I don't mind spending more time doing that now than in the past.
lines.cn: F：我喜欢教学，而且我不介意现在比过去花更多时间在这上面。

lines.t: F: Also, what I will say is that teaching a subject helps me comprehend it better myself.
lines.cn: F：另外，我要说的是，讲授一门学科能帮助我自己更好地理解它。

lines.t: F: I find that it furthers my own knowledge when I have to explain something clearly, when I have to aid others in understanding it, and when I have to answer questions about it.
lines.cn: F：我发现，当我必须清楚地解释某件事、必须帮助别人理解它、必须回答关于它的提问时，我自己的知识也会更进一步。

lines.t: F: Teaching at a high level can be very stimulating for anyone, no matter how much expertise they may already have in the field they are instructing.
lines.cn: F：高水平的教学对任何人都能带来很强的激励，无论他们在所教授的领域已有多深的专业造诣。

lines.t: M: Of any scientific breakthroughs that you see on the near horizon, a significant discovery or invention we can expect soon.
lines.cn: M：在不远的将来你看得到的科学突破中，有没有我们很快可以期待的重大发现或发明？

lines.t: F: The world is always conducting science, and there are constantly new things being discovered.
lines.cn: F：世界一直在进行科学研究，新发现层出不穷。

lines.t: F: In fact, right now we have too much data sitting in computers.
lines.cn: F：事实上，现在有太多的数据堆在计算机里。

lines.t: F: For example, we have thousands of photos of planet Mars taken by telescopes that nobody has ever seen.
lines.cn: F：例如，我们有数千张望远镜拍摄的火星照片，从来没有人看过。

lines.t: F: We have them, but nobody has had time to look at them with their own eyes, let alone analyze them.
lines.cn: F：我们拥有它们，但没有人有时间亲眼看看它们，更别说分析它们了。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do both speakers think of dreams?

options.A: They can predict future events.
options.B: They have no special meanings.
options.C: They have cultural connotations.
options.D: They cannot be easily explained.

questions.cn: 两位说话人都怎么看梦？

optionsCn.A: 它们能预测未来事件。
optionsCn.B: 它们没有特殊含义。
optionsCn.C: 它们有文化内涵。
optionsCn.D: 它们无法轻易解释。

questions.stem: Why didn't the woman's grandmother take her scheduled flight?

options.A: It was canceled due to bad weather.
options.B: She overslept and missed the flight.
options.C: She dreamed of a plane crash.
options.D: It was postponed to the following day.

questions.cn: 女士的祖母为什么没有坐原定的航班？

optionsCn.A: 航班因恶劣天气取消。
optionsCn.B: 她睡过头错过了航班。
optionsCn.C: 她梦见飞机坠毁。
optionsCn.D: 航班被推迟到第二天。

questions.stem: What does the woman say about people's emotions?

options.A: They can be affected by people's childhood experiences.
options.B: They may sometimes seem ridiculous to a rational mind.
options.C: They usually result from people's unpleasant memories.
options.D: They can have an impact as great as rational thinking.

questions.cn: 关于人的情绪，女士说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们会受童年经历影响。
optionsCn.B: 它们有时在理性头脑看来显得荒唐。
optionsCn.C: 它们通常源自人们不愉快的记忆。
optionsCn.D: 它们的影响可以与理性思维一样大。

questions.stem: What did psychologist Sigmund Freud say about adults' dreams?

options.A: They call for scientific methods to interpret.
options.B: They mirror their long-cherished wishes.
options.C: They reflect their complicated emotions.
options.D: They are often related to irrational feelings.

questions.cn: 心理学家西格蒙德·弗洛伊德关于成人的梦说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们需要科学方法来解读。
optionsCn.B: 它们映照出他们长久以来的愿望。
optionsCn.C: 它们反映出他们复杂的情绪。
optionsCn.D: 它们常常与非理性的感受有关。

lines.t: Conversation two
lines.cn: 对话二。

lines.t: M: Do you think dreams have special meanings?
lines.cn: M：你认为梦有特殊的含义吗？

lines.t: F: No, I don't think they do.
lines.cn: F：不，我不这么认为。

lines.t: M: I don't either, but some people do.
lines.cn: M：我也不认为，但有些人认为有。

lines.t: M: I would say people who believe that dreams have special meanings are superstitious, especially nowadays.
lines.cn: M：我想，认为梦有特殊含义的人是迷信的，尤其在如今这个时代。

lines.t: M: In the past, during the times of ancient Egypt, Greece or China, people used to believe that dreams could foresee the future.
lines.cn: M：在过去，在古埃及、古希腊或中国，人们曾经相信梦能预见未来。

lines.t: M: But today, with all the scientific knowledge that we have, I think it's much harder to believe in these sorts of things.
lines.cn: M：但今天，有了我们所掌握的全部科学知识，我觉得再相信这类事情就难得多了。

lines.t: F: My grandmother is superstitious, and she thinks dreams can predict the future.
lines.cn: F：我祖母很迷信，她认为梦能预测未来。

lines.t: F: Once, she dreamed that the flight she was due to take the following day crashed.
lines.cn: F：有一次，她梦见自己第二天要坐的航班坠毁了。

lines.t: F: Can you guess what she did?
lines.cn: F：你猜她做了什么？

lines.t: F: She didn't take that flight.
lines.cn: F：她没有坐那一班。

lines.t: F: She didn't even bother to go to the airport the following day.
lines.cn: F：第二天她连机场都没去。

lines.t: F: Instead, she took the same flight, but a week later.
lines.cn: F：相反，她坐了同一个航班，但在一周之后。

lines.t: F: And everything was fine, of course.
lines.cn: F：当然，一切正常。

lines.t: F: No plane ever crashed.
lines.cn: F：没有任何飞机坠毁。

lines.t: M: How funny.
lines.cn: M：真有意思。

lines.t: M: Did you know that flying is actually safer than any other mode of transport?
lines.cn: M：你知道吗，坐飞机其实比任何其他交通方式都安全。

lines.t: M: It's been statistically proven.
lines.cn: M：这在统计上已被证明。

lines.t: M: People can be so irrational sometimes.
lines.cn: M：人们有时候确实很不理性。

lines.t: F: Yes, absolutely.
lines.cn: F：是的，绝对如此。

lines.t: F: But even if we think they're ridiculous, emotions can be just as powerful as rational thinking.
lines.cn: F：但即使我们觉得那些事很荒唐，情绪也可能和理性思维一样强大。

lines.t: M: Exactly.
lines.cn: M：正是。

lines.t: M: People do all sorts of crazy things because of their irrational feelings.
lines.cn: M：人们因为不理性的感受而做出各种疯狂的事情。

lines.t: F: But in fact, some psychologists believe that our dreams are the result of our emotions and memories from that day.
lines.cn: F：但实际上，一些心理学家认为，梦是我们当天的情绪和记忆的结果。

lines.t: F: I think it was Sigmund Freud who said that children's dreams were usually simple representations of their wishes, things they wish would happen.
lines.cn: F：我想是西格蒙德·弗洛伊德说过：儿童的梦通常是他们愿望的简单呈现，是他们希望发生的事。

lines.t: F: But in adults, dreams are much more complicated reflections of their more sophisticated sentiments.
lines.cn: F：而成年人的梦，则是其更复杂情感的要复杂得多的映照。

lines.t: M: Isn't it interesting how psychologists try to understand, using the scientific method, something as bizarre as dreams?
lines.cn: M：有趣的是，心理学家用科学方法试图理解像梦这样离奇的东西。

lines.t: M: Psychology is like the rational study of irrational feelings.
lines.cn: M：心理学就像是对非理性感受进行的理性研究。

tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What did scientists first use to discover Lake Vostok in the 1970s?

options.A: Radio waves.
options.B: Sound waves.
options.C: Robots.
options.D: Satellites.

questions.cn: 科学家在 20 世纪 70 年代最初用什么发现了沃斯托克湖？

optionsCn.A: 无线电波。
optionsCn.B: 声波。
optionsCn.C: 机器人。
optionsCn.D: 卫星。

questions.stem: What do scientists think about Lake Vostok?

options.A: It may be freezing fast beneath the glacier.
options.B: It may have micro-organisms living in it.
options.C: It may have certain rare minerals in it.
options.D: It may be as deep as four kilometers.

questions.cn: 科学家如何看待沃斯托克湖？

optionsCn.A: 它在冰川下正快速冻结。
optionsCn.B: 它可能有微生物生活在其中。
optionsCn.C: 它里面可能含有某些稀有矿物。
optionsCn.D: 它的深度可能达四公里。

questions.stem: What do the scientists hope their discoveries will do?

options.A: Help understand life in freezing conditions.
options.B: Help find new sources of fresh water.
options.C: Provide information about other planets.
options.D: Shed light on possible life in outer space.

questions.cn: 科学家希望他们的发现能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 帮助理解严寒条件下的生命。
optionsCn.B: 帮助寻找新的淡水资源。
optionsCn.C: 提供关于其他行星的信息。
optionsCn.D: 照亮外太空可能存在的生命。

lines.t: Passage 1.
lines.cn: 短文一。

lines.t: While some scientists explore the surface of Antarctica, others are learning more about a giant body of water four kilometers beneath the ice pack.
lines.cn: 当一些科学家探索南极洲表面时，另一些正在研究冰盖四公里以下的一块巨大的水体。

lines.t: Scientists first discovered Lake Vostok in the 1970s by using radio waves that penetrate the ice.
lines.cn: 科学家在 20 世纪 70 年代首次借助能穿透冰层的无线电波发现了沃斯托克湖。

lines.t: Since then, they have used sound waves and even satellites to map this massive body of water.
lines.cn: 从那以后，他们又用声波甚至卫星来绘制这片巨大水体的地图。

lines.t: How does the water in Lake Vostok remain liquid beneath an ice sheet?
lines.cn: 沃斯托克湖的水在冰盖之下如何保持液态？

lines.t: The thick glacier above acts like an insulating blanket and keeps the water from freezing, says Martin Siegert, a glaciologist from the University of Wales.
lines.cn: 威尔士大学的冰川学家马丁·西格特说，上方厚厚的冰川像一层隔热毯，使湖水不致冻结。

lines.t: In addition, geothermal heat from deep within the earth may warm the hidden lake.
lines.cn: 此外，来自地球深部的地热也可能为这个隐秘的湖泊加热。

lines.t: The scientists suspect that microorganisms may be living in Lake Vostok, closed off from the outside world for more than two million years.
lines.cn: 科学家怀疑，微生物可能就生活在这个与外界隔绝超过 200 万年的湖里。

lines.t: Anything found there will be totally alien to what's on the surface of the earth, says Siegert.
lines.cn: 西格特说，在那里发现的任何东西，都将与地球表面的生物完全不同。

lines.t: Scientists are trying to find a way to drill into the ice and draw water samples without causing contamination.
lines.cn: 科学家正在设法钻入冰层并提取水样，同时不造成污染。

lines.t: Again, robots might be the solution.
lines.cn: 同样，机器人也许是解决方案。

lines.t: If all goes as planned, a drill-shaped robot will melt through the surface ice.
lines.cn: 如果一切按计划进行，一个钻头形状的机器人将融化表层冰。

lines.t: When it reaches the lake, it will release another robot that can swim in the lake, take pictures, and look for signs of life.
lines.cn: 到达湖中后，它会释放出另一个能在湖里游动、拍照并寻找生命迹象的机器人。

lines.t: The scientists hope their discoveries will shed light on life in outer space, which might exist in similar dark and arid conditions.
lines.cn: 科学家希望他们的发现能照亮外太空的生命问题——那或许也存在于类似的黑暗干旱条件下。

lines.t: Recently, close-up pictures of Jupiter's moon Europa showed signs of water beneath its icy surface.
lines.cn: 最近，木星卫星欧罗巴的近距离照片显示，其冰面之下存在水的迹象。

lines.t: Once tested in Antarctica, robots could be sent to Europa to search for life there, too.
lines.cn: 一旦在南极完成测试，机器人也可以被送往欧罗巴寻找那里的生命。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: Why did James Copeland want to study the American Indian tribe, Tarahumaras?

options.A: He found there had been little research on their language.
options.B: He was trying to preserve the languages of the Indian tribes.
options.C: His contact with a social worker had greatly aroused his interest in the tribe.
options.D: His meeting with Gonzalez had made him eager to learn more about the tribe.

questions.cn: 詹姆斯·科普兰为什么想研究美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人？

optionsCn.A: 他发现对他们的语言几乎没有任何研究。
optionsCn.B: 他试图保护印第安部落的语言。
optionsCn.C: 他与一位社会工作者的接触大大激发了他对部落的兴趣。
optionsCn.D: 他与贡萨莱斯的会面让他渴望更多地了解这个部落。

questions.stem: How did Gonzalez help James Copeland?

options.A: He taught Copeland to speak the Tarahumaras language.
options.B: He persuaded the Tarahumaras to accept Copeland's gifts.
options.C: He recommended one of his best friends as an interpreter.
options.D: He acted as an intermediary between Copeland and the villagers.

questions.cn: 贡萨莱斯怎样帮助詹姆斯·科普兰？

optionsCn.A: 他教科普兰说塔拉乌马拉语。
optionsCn.B: 他说服塔拉乌马拉人接受科普兰的礼物。
optionsCn.C: 他推荐了自己最好的朋友做翻译。
optionsCn.D: 他在科普兰和村民之间充当中间人。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about James Copeland's trip to the Tarahumaras village?

options.A: Unpredictable.
options.B: Unjustifiable.
options.C: Laborious.
options.D: Tedious.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何评价詹姆斯·科普兰去塔拉乌马拉村庄的旅程？

optionsCn.A: 难以预料。
optionsCn.B: 不正当。
optionsCn.C: 费力。
optionsCn.D: 乏味。

questions.stem: What impresses James Copeland about the Tarahumaras tribe?

options.A: Their appreciation of help from the outsiders.
options.B: Their sense of sharing and caring.
options.C: Their readiness to adapt to technology.
options.D: Their belief in creating wealth for themselves.

questions.cn: 塔拉乌马拉部落给詹姆斯·科普兰留下深刻印象的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们对外来帮助的感激。
optionsCn.B: 他们的分享与关怀意识。
optionsCn.C: 他们适应技术的意愿。
optionsCn.D: 他们为自己创造财富的信念。

lines.t: Passage 2.
lines.cn: 短文二。

lines.t: The idea to study the American Indian tribe Tarahumaras came to James Copeland in 1984 when he discovered that very little research had been done on their language.
lines.cn: 1984 年，詹姆斯·科普兰萌生了研究美洲印第安部落塔拉乌马拉人的想法，因为他发现对他们的语言几乎没有任何研究。

lines.t: He contacted a tribe member through a social worker who worked with the tribesmen in Mexico.
lines.cn: 他通过一位在墨西哥与部落成员共事的社会工作者，联系上了一位部落成员。

lines.t: At first, the tribe member, named Gonzales, was very reluctant to cooperate.
lines.cn: 起初，这位名叫贡萨莱斯的部落成员非常不愿意合作。

lines.t: He told Copeland that no amount of money could buy his language.
lines.cn: 他告诉科普兰，再多的钱也买不到他的语言。

lines.t: But after Copeland explained to him what he intended to do with his research, and how it would benefit the Tarahumaras, Gonzales agreed to help.
lines.cn: 但在科普兰向他解释了研究打算做什么、以及它将如何惠及塔拉乌马拉人之后，贡萨莱斯同意帮忙。

lines.t: He took Copeland to his village and served as an intermediary.
lines.cn: 他把科普兰带回村庄，并担任中间人。

lines.t: Copeland says, thanks to him, the Tarahumaras understood what our mission was and started trusting us.
lines.cn: 科普兰说，多亏了他，塔拉乌马拉人才明白我们的使命是什么，并开始信任我们。

lines.t: Entering the world of the Tarahumaras has been a laborious project for Copeland.
lines.cn: 进入塔拉乌马拉人的世界，对科普兰来说是一项费力的工程。

lines.t: To reach their homeland, he must drive two and a half days from Houston, Texas.
lines.cn: 要抵达他们的家园，他必须从得克萨斯州休斯敦开车两天半。

lines.t: He loads up his vehicle with goods that the tribesmen can't easily get, and gives the goods to them as a gesture of friendship.
lines.cn: 他往车上装满部落成员不易得到的东西，并把它们作为友谊的表示送给他们。

lines.t: The Tarahumaras, who don't believe in accumulating wealth, take the food and share it among themselves.
lines.cn: 不信奉积累财富的塔拉乌马拉人收下食物后彼此分享。

lines.t: For Copeland, the experience has not only been academically satisfying, it also has enriched his life in several ways.
lines.cn: 对科普兰来说，这段经历不仅带来学术上的满足，还在多个方面丰富了他的生活。

lines.t: I see people rejecting technology and living a very hard, traditional life, which offers me another notion about the meaning of progress in the tradition, he says.
lines.cn: 他说，我看到人们拒绝技术、过着非常艰难的传统生活，这让我对传统中的“进步”意味着什么有了另一种认识。

lines.t: I experience the simplicity of living in nature that I would otherwise only be able to read about.
lines.cn: 我体验了在自然中生活的简朴——否则我只能从书本上读到它。

lines.t: I see a lot of beauty in their sense of sharing and concern for each other.
lines.cn: 我从他们分享和彼此关怀的感觉中，看到了许多美。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What usually happens when people are accused of being radical?

options.A: They tend to be silenced into submission.
options.B: They find it hard to defend themselves.
options.C: They will feel proud of being pioneers.
options.D: They will feel somewhat encouraged.

questions.cn: 当人们被指责为激进者时通常会怎样？

optionsCn.A: 他们往往被压服而沉默。
optionsCn.B: 他们发现难以为自己辩护。
optionsCn.C: 他们会为成为先驱而自豪。
optionsCn.D: 他们会受到些许鼓舞。

questions.stem: What is the speaker's definition of a radical?

options.A: One who advocates violence in effecting change.
options.B: One who craves for relentless transformations.
options.C: One who acts in the interests of the oppressed.
options.D: One who rebels against the existing social order.

questions.cn: 讲话者对“激进者”的定义是什么？

optionsCn.A: 以暴力促成变革的人。
optionsCn.B: 渴望无情变革的人。
optionsCn.C: 为受压迫者的利益而行动的人。
optionsCn.D: 反抗现有社会秩序的人。

questions.stem: What does the speaker think of most radicals in the American history?

options.A: They tried to effect social change by force.
options.B: They disrupted the nation's social stability.
options.C: They served as a driving force for progress.
options.D: They did more harm than good to humanity.

questions.cn: 讲话者如何看待美国历史上大多数的激进者？

optionsCn.A: 他们试图用暴力推动社会变革。
optionsCn.B: 他们破坏了国家的社会稳定。
optionsCn.C: 他们是进步的推动力。
optionsCn.D: 他们对人类弊大于利。

lines.t: Followed by three or four questions.
lines.cn: 后接三到四个问题。

lines.t: Recording 1.
lines.cn: 录音一。

lines.t: What is a radical?
lines.cn: 什么是激进者？

lines.t: It seems today that people are terrified of the term, particularly of having the label attached to them.
lines.cn: 今天看来，人们对这个词感到恐惧，尤其害怕被贴上这个标签。

lines.t: Accusing individuals or groups of being radical often serves to silence them into submission, thereby maintaining the existing state of affairs and, more important, preserving the power of a select minority who are mostly wealthy white male in Western society.
lines.cn: 指责个人或群体为激进者，往往能让他们沉默顺服，从而维持现状，更重要的是，保住被选中的少数人的权力——在西方社会，他们大多是有钱的白人男性。

lines.t: Feminism is a perfect example of this phenomenon.
lines.cn: 女权主义就是这一现象的绝佳例证。

lines.t: The women's movement has been plagued by stereotypes, misrepresentations by the media, and accusations of man-hating and radicalism, when the basic foundation of feminism is simply that women deserve equal rights in all facets of life.
lines.cn: 妇女运动长期被刻板印象、媒体的歪曲，以及“仇男”和“激进”的指责所困扰，而女权主义的根本基础其实很简单：女性在生活的各个方面都应享有平等权利。

lines.t: When faced with the threat of being labeled radical, women back down from their worthy cause and consequently participate in their own oppression.
lines.cn: 当面临被贴上“激进”标签的威胁时，女性从她们正当的事业面前退却，从而参与了对自身的压迫。

lines.t: It has gotten to the point that many women are afraid to call themselves feminists because of the stigma attached to the word.
lines.cn: 已经到了这种地步：许多女性不敢自称女权主义者，因为这个词被烙上了污名。

lines.t: If people refuse to be controlled and intimidated by stigmas, the stigmas lose all their power.
lines.cn: 如果人们拒绝被污名所控制和恐吓，污名就会失去全部力量。

lines.t: Without fear on which to feed, such stigmas can only die.
lines.cn: 没有了可供其吞噬的恐惧，这样的污名只能消亡。

lines.t: To me, a radical is simply someone who rebels against the norm or advocates a change in the existing state of affairs.
lines.cn: 对我来说，激进者不过是一个反抗常规、或倡导改变现状的人。

lines.t: On closer inspection, it becomes clear that the norm is constantly evolving and therefore is not a constant entity.
lines.cn: 细看之下就会发现，“常规”本身在不断演变，因此并非恒定之物。

lines.t: So why then is deviation from the present situation such a threat when the state of affairs itself is unstable and subject to relentless transformation?
lines.cn: 那么，既然现状本身就不稳定、正被无情地改变着，偏离现状又为何是一种威胁呢？

lines.t: It all goes back to maintaining the power of those who have it and preventing the rise of those who don't.
lines.cn: 一切都要回到“维护掌权者的权力、阻止无权者崛起”这一点上。

lines.t: In fact, when we look at the word radical in a historical context, nearly every figure we now hold up as a hero was considered a radical in his or her time.
lines.cn: 事实上，当我们把“激进”一词放进历史语境中看，如今被我们奉为英雄的几乎每一个人，在他或她所处的时代都被视为激进者。

lines.t: Radicals are people who affect change.
lines.cn: 激进者是带来改变的人。

lines.t: They are the people about whom history is written.
lines.cn: 他们是历史书写所围绕的人。

lines.t: Abolitionists were radicals.
lines.cn: 废奴主义者是激进者。

lines.t: Civil rights activists were radicals.
lines.cn: 民权活动家是激进者。

lines.t: Even the founders of our country in their fight to win independence from England were radicals.
lines.cn: 甚至我们国家的建国者，在为摆脱英国、赢得独立而斗争时，也是激进者。

lines.t: Their presence in history has changed the way our society functions, mainly by shifting the balance of power that previously existed.
lines.cn: 他们在历史上的存在改变了我们社会运转的方式，主要是改变了先前存在的权力平衡。

lines.t: Of course, there are some radicals who've made a negative impact on humanity, but undeniably there would simply be no progress without radicals.
lines.cn: 当然，也有一些激进者给人类带来了负面影响，但不可否认，没有激进者，就不会有任何进步。

lines.t: That being said, next time someone calls me a radical, I will accept that label with pride.
lines.cn: 话虽如此，下次有人叫我激进者时，我会骄傲地接受这个标签。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about us as human beings?

options.A: Few of us can ignore changes in our immediate environment.
options.B: It is impossible for us to be immune from outside influence.
options.C: Few of us can remain unaware of what happens around us.
options.D: It is important for us to keep in touch with our own world.

questions.cn: 作为人类，讲话者对我们说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 我们中很少有人能忽视身边环境的变化。
optionsCn.B: 我们不可能不受外界影响。
optionsCn.C: 我们中很少有人能对周围发生的事毫无察觉。
optionsCn.D: 与自己的世界保持联系对我们很重要。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say Fred should do first to improve his quality of life?

options.A: Make up his mind to start all over again.
options.B: Stop making unfair judgements of others.
options.C: Try to find a more exciting job somewhere else.
options.D: Recognise the negative impact of his coworkers.

questions.cn: 讲话者说弗雷德改善生活质量首先应该做什么？

optionsCn.A: 下定决心从头再来。
optionsCn.B: 停止对他人做不公正的评判。
optionsCn.C: 尝试在别处找一份更刺激的工作。
optionsCn.D: 认清同事带来的负面影响。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about psychiatrists?

options.A: They are quite susceptible to suicide.
options.B: They improve people's quality of life.
options.C: They suffer a great deal from ill health.
options.D: They help people solve mental problems.

questions.cn: 关于精神科医生，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们很容易自杀。
optionsCn.B: 他们改善人们的生活质量。
optionsCn.C: 他们受健康状况不佳的折磨。
optionsCn.D: 他们帮助人们解决心理问题。

lines.t: Recording 2.
lines.cn: 录音二。

lines.t: We are very susceptible to the influence of the people around us.
lines.cn: 我们非常容易受周围人的影响。

lines.t: For instance, you may have known somebody who has gone overseas for a year or so and has returned with an accent perhaps.
lines.cn: 例如，你可能认识这样的人：出国一年左右，回来时带上了口音。

lines.t: We become part of our immediate environment.
lines.cn: 我们会成为身边环境的一部分。

lines.t: None of us are immune to the influences of our own world and let us not kid ourselves that we are untouched by the things and the people in our life.
lines.cn: 没有人能对我们所处世界的影响免疫，我们也别自欺欺人地说自己不受生活中事物和人的影响。

lines.t: Fred goes off to his new job at a factory.
lines.cn: 弗雷德去工厂开始了他的新工作。

lines.t: Fred takes a 10-minute coffee break, but the other workers take a half an hour.
lines.cn: 弗雷德喝 10 分钟咖啡休息，而其他工人休息半小时。

lines.t: Fred says, what's the matter with you guys?
lines.cn: 弗雷德说：“你们这些人怎么回事？”

lines.t: Weeks later, Fred is taking 20-minute breaks.
lines.cn: 几周后，弗雷德开始休息 20 分钟。

lines.t: A month later, Fred takes his half hour.
lines.cn: 一个月后，弗雷德休息半小时了。

lines.t: Fred is saying, if you can't beat them, join them.
lines.cn: 弗雷德在说：如果你打不过他们，就加入他们。

lines.t: Why would I work any harder than the next guy?
lines.cn: 我为什么要比旁边的人更卖力？

lines.t: The fascinating thing about being human is that generally we are unaware that there are changes taking place in our mentality.
lines.cn: 身为人类的迷人之处在于，我们通常意识不到自己的心态正在发生变化。

lines.t: It is like returning to the city smog after some weeks in the fresh air.
lines.cn: 这就像在新鲜空气中待了几周后回到满是雾霾的城市。

lines.t: Only then do we realize that we have become accustomed to the nasty smells.
lines.cn: 只有那时我们才意识到，自己已经习惯了那些难闻的气味。

lines.t: Mix with critical people and we learn to criticize.
lines.cn: 和爱挑剔的人混在一起，我们就学会了挑剔。

lines.t: Mix with happy people and we learn about happiness.
lines.cn: 和快乐的人混在一起，我们就学会快乐。

lines.t: What this means is that we need to decide what we want from life and then choose our company accordingly.
lines.cn: 这意味着，我们需要决定自己想从生活中得到什么，然后据此选择自己的同伴。

lines.t: You may well say, that is going to take some effort.
lines.cn: 你完全可以说：那要花些功夫。

lines.t: It may not be comfortable.
lines.cn: 它可能让人不舒服。

lines.t: I may offend some of my present company.
lines.cn: 我可能会冒犯现在的某些伙伴。

lines.t: Right, but it is your life.
lines.cn: 没错，但这是你的人生。

lines.t: Fred may say, I'm always broke, frequently depressed, I'm going nowhere, and I never do anything exciting.
lines.cn: 弗雷德也许会说：我总是缺钱，经常情绪低落，我哪儿也去不了，我从没做过什么刺激的事。

lines.t: Then we discover that Fred's best friends are always broke, frequently depressed, going nowhere, and wishing that life was more exciting.
lines.cn: 然后我们发现，弗雷德最好的朋友们也总是缺钱、经常低落、哪儿也去不了、盼着生活更刺激。

lines.t: This is not coincidence, nor is it our business to stand in judgment of Fred.
lines.cn: 这不是巧合，评判弗雷德也不是我们的事。

lines.t: However, if Fred wants to improve his quality of life, the first thing he'll need to do is recognize what has been going on all these years.
lines.cn: 然而，如果弗雷德想改善自己的生活质量，他需要做的第一件事，就是认清这些年来发生的一切。

lines.t: It's no surprise that doctors, as a profession, suffer a lot of ill health because they spend their lives around sick people.
lines.cn: 医生这个职业自身健康状况不好的人很多，这并不奇怪，因为他们一生都围着病人转。

lines.t: Psychiatrists have a higher incidence of suicide in their profession for related reasons.
lines.cn: 出于相关原因，精神科医生的职业里自杀率更高。

lines.t: Traditionally, nine out of ten children whose parents smoke, smoke themselves.
lines.cn: 传统上，父母吸烟的孩子十个有九个自己也吸烟。

lines.t: Obesity is in part an environmental problem.
lines.cn: 肥胖在部分程度上是一个环境问题。

lines.t: Successful people are successful friends and so the story goes on.
lines.cn: 成功的人拥有成功的朋友，故事就这样延续下去。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the American dollar bill?

options.A: Few people can identify its texture.
options.B: Few people can describe it precisely.
options.C: Its real value is open to interpretation.
options.D: Its importance is often over-estimated.

questions.cn: 关于美元纸币，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 很少有人能辨认出它的手感。
optionsCn.B: 很少有人能准确描述它。
optionsCn.C: 它的真实价值可以有不同的解释。
optionsCn.D: 它的重要性常被高估。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say about the exact composition of the American dollar bill?

options.A: It has never seen any change.
options.B: It has much to do with color.
options.C: It is a well-protected government secret.
options.D: It is a subject of study by many forgers.

questions.cn: 关于美元纸币的确切成分，讲话者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它从未有任何变化。
optionsCn.B: 它与颜色有很大关系。
optionsCn.C: 它是一个被严密保护的政府机密。
optionsCn.D: 它是许多造假者研究的课题。

questions.stem: Why did the new American government mint only coins for common currency?

options.A: People had little faith in paper money.
options.B: They could last longer in circulation.
options.C: It predicted their value would increase.
options.D: They were more difficult to counterfeit.

questions.cn: 新生的美国政府为什么只为通用货币铸造硬币？

optionsCn.A: 人们对纸币没有多少信心。
optionsCn.B: 它们在流通中能存续更久。
optionsCn.C: 它预计它们的价值会上涨。
optionsCn.D: 它们更难伪造。

questions.stem: What have generations of American politicians argued for?

options.A: The stabilization of the dollar value.
options.B: The issuing of government securities.
options.C: A gold standard for American currency.
options.D: A steady appreciation of the U.S. dollar.

questions.cn: 一代代美国政治家主张的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 稳定美元价值。
optionsCn.B: 发行政府证券。
optionsCn.C: 美国货币实行金本位。
optionsCn.D: 美元稳步升值。

lines.t: Recording 3.
lines.cn: 录音三。

lines.t: Virtually every American can recognize a dollar bill at a mere glance.
lines.cn: 几乎每个美国人都能一眼认出一张美元纸币。

lines.t: Many can identify it by its sound or texture, but few people indeed can accurately describe the world's most powerful important currency.
lines.cn: 许多人能凭声音或手感认出它，但真正能准确描述这种世界上最强大、最重要的货币的人却很少。

lines.t: The American dollar bill is colored with black ink on one side and green on the other.
lines.cn: 美元纸币一面印黑色油墨，另一面印绿色。

lines.t: The exact composition of the paper and ink is a closely guarded government secret.
lines.cn: 纸张和油墨的确切成分是一个被严密守护的政府机密。

lines.t: Despite its weighty importance, the dollar bill actually weighs little.
lines.cn: 尽管地位举足轻重，美元纸币其实很轻。

lines.t: It requires nearly 500 bills to tip the scales at a pound.
lines.cn: 要凑够一磅重，需要近 500 张纸币。

lines.t: Not only is the dollar bill lightweight, but it also has a brief lifespan.
lines.cn: 美元纸币不仅轻，而且寿命不长。

lines.t: Few dollar bills survive longer than 18 months.
lines.cn: 很少有纸币能存续超过 18 个月。

lines.t: The word dollar is taken from the German word Tala, the name for the world's most important currency in the 16th century.
lines.cn: “美元”一词取自德语词“塔勒”，那是 16 世纪世界上最重要的货币的名字。

lines.t: The Tala was a silver coin first minted in 1518 under the reign of Charles V, Emperor of Germany.
lines.cn: 塔勒是一种银币，1518 年在德意志皇帝查理五世统治时期首次铸造。

lines.t: The concept of paper money is a relatively recent innovation in the history of American currency.
lines.cn: 纸币的概念，在美国货币史上是相对晚近的发明。

lines.t: When the constitution was signed, people had little regard for paper money because of its steadily decreasing value during the colonial era.
lines.cn: 宪法签署时，人们对纸币不太信任，因为殖民地时期纸币的价值不断下降。

lines.t: Because of this lack of faith, the new American government minted many coins for common currency.
lines.cn: 由于这种不信任，新生的美国政府为通用货币铸造了许多硬币。

lines.t: Interest-bearing banknotes were issued at the same time, but their purpose was limited to providing money for urgent government crises, such as American involvement in the War of 1812.
lines.cn: 附息银行券也同时发行，但其用途仅限于为紧急的政府危机提供资金，比如美国卷入 1812 年战争。

lines.t: The first non-interest-bearing paper currency was authorized by Congress in 1862 at the height of the Civil War.
lines.cn: 第一张不计息的纸币是国会在 1862 年内战正酣时授权发行的。

lines.t: At this point, citizens' old fears of devalued paper currency had calmed, and the dollar bill was born.
lines.cn: 此时，民众对贬值纸币的旧日恐惧已经平息，美元纸币由此诞生。

lines.t: The new green-colored paper money quickly earned the name greenback.
lines.cn: 这种绿色的新纸币很快赢得了“绿钞”的名字。

lines.t: Today, the American dollar bill is a product of the Federal Reserve and is issued from the twelve Federal Reserve banks around the United States.
lines.cn: 如今，美元纸币是联邦储备系统的产品，由美国各地的十二家联邦储备银行发行。

lines.t: The government keeps a steady supply of approximately two billion bills in circulation at all times.
lines.cn: 政府始终保持约 20 亿张纸币的稳定流通量。

lines.t: Controversy continues to surround the true value of the dollar bill.
lines.cn: 关于美元纸币真实价值的争论至今仍在继续。

lines.t: American history has seen generations of politicians argue in favor of a gold standard for American currency.
lines.cn: 美国历史上，代代政治家都主张美国货币应实行金本位。

lines.t: However, for the present, the American dollar bill holds the value that is printed on it, and little more.
lines.cn: 不过就目前而言，美元纸币承载的只是印在上面的价值，仅此而已。

lines.t: The only other guarantee on the bill is a Federal Reserve pledge as a confirmation in the form of government securities.
lines.cn: 纸币上唯一的另一种担保，是美联储以政府证券形式作出的一纸承诺。
